name: Poland
tagline: Cheap, big, and more free English-taught places than you think
ownCitizens: If you hold Polish citizenship, article 324 of the Higher Education Act — the source of this page's rules for foreigners — does not apply to you: Polish-taught study is free, and the maintenance grant and student loan are open to you on the ordinary terms. Your IB is still a foreign qualification, so the IB entry rules here still apply, and whether you count as a foreign candidate at universities with a separate foreigners' recruitment, such as Wroclaw Tech, is not established here: ask them.
summary: Poland recognises an IB Diploma automatically — no recognition statement needed — and has a large, affordable English-taught offer, from engineering in Kraków and Wrocław to medicine in Gdańsk and Poznań. You apply directly to each university on its own system and calendar. Polish-taught study is free for EU citizens; English-taught fees vary by programme, and some are free for EU citizens too.
whyConsider: Your IB Diploma is automatically recognised for applying to university.
A large English-taught offer at modest fees, including six-year medicine.
Some English-taught programmes cost EU citizens nothing — check each programme's fee line.
watchOuts: No central portal and no national deadline. Each university sets its own, and most had not published 2027 dates by September 2026.
HL versus SL matters more than your total. Universities convert them very differently, and some programmes require a science at HL.

If you plan to practise in Denmark, studying medicine here involves more than the diploma — read the medicine-abroad page before committing. Wherever you plan to practise, check how that country recognises the degree.

notes: NAWA, the recognition body, states that IB certificates are automatically recognised for applying to first-cycle and long-cycle studies, with no individual recognition statement. Each university then applies its own conversion of IB grades.

language.englishProof: An IB Diploma taught in English is usually accepted. Confirm per university; some medical schools want IELTS.

feeContext.summary: Full-time Polish-taught study at a state university is free for EU/EEA citizens. English-taught programmes vary: at the University of Warsaw some are free for EU citizens and others charge several thousand euros a year.

sectorLandscape.summary: Poland divides its higher education into university-type institutions (uczelnia akademicka), which do research and can award doctorates, and non-university institutions (uczelnia zawodowa), which teach practically oriented bachelor's programmes. Medical universities and art academies are separate public institutions, and there is a large private (niepubliczna) sector.

routes.what: Universities and technical universities (politechnika) — Warsaw, Jagiellonian, AGH, Wrocław Tech and others. Most English-taught bachelor's are here.
Practice-oriented institutions offering bachelor's degrees (licencjat or inżynier). The kind of place nobody mentions to foreigners.
Public medical universities, several with six-year English-taught medicine and dentistry.
Fine art, music, theatre and film, admitting on portfolio or audition.
A large private sector, mostly business and social sciences, including Kozminski University.

notes: Most 2027 university calendars were not published by September 2026; the country profile carries 2026 dates as provisional.
Not established: which uczelnie zawodowe teach in English.
'uczelnia medyczna' and 'uczelnia artystyczna' are ordinary Polish descriptive terms; the Eurydice page read names these categories in English ('a medical HEI', 'an HEI of art studies').
The PUMS class-start contradiction (country profile, ev-pums-calendar-class-start) is still open.
